2026 年企业 LLM Agent 平台选型

Executive Summary

DeepAgents is a LangChain harness built on LangGraph. It provides planning, sub-agents, a filesystem abstraction, and human-in-the-loop controls. For RefractRouter v0.1, DeepAgents is useful as the fixed-DAG execution harness, but its autonomous planning and dynamic sub-agent generation should remain disabled. [source_001]

Background

LangGraph is a graph state machine framework for complex workflows. It supports explicit nodes, edges, durable state, and check-pointing. RefractRouter uses LangGraph as the lower-level execution substrate for a fixed task DAG. [source_002]

Selection Criteria

Pydantic AI provides typed tool definitions and structured model outputs. It is useful when strict schemas are required, but RefractRouter v0.1 does not need it as a core dependency unless structured-output parsing becomes a bottleneck. [source_003]

Platform Comparison

DeepSeek Harness, or DSH, is an agent harness where the agent loop itself is a plugin. For RefractRouter v0.1, DSH is reserved for the outer validation environment, not the core routing loop. [source_004]

Risks

Existing LLM routing work mostly selects one model for an entire request. RefractRouter studies whether selecting a model separately for each node in a task DAG can improve the quality-cost-latency Pareto frontier. [source_005]

Conclusion

Static task decomposition belongs to the application layer. The router receives the DAG as input and focuses on per-node model selection. Dynamic re-splitting is deferred until node-level routing is validated. [source_006]

References

A useful routing benchmark needs fixed task DAGs, multiple candidate models, per-node and per-task scoring, cost accounting, and critical-path latency. The first benchmark should stay small enough to reproduce. [source_007]

For RefractRouter v0.1, DeepAgents is useful as the fixed-DAG execution harness, but its autonomous planning and dynamic sub-agent generation should remain disabled.
  2. LangGraph: LangGraph is a graph state machine framework for complex workflows. It supports explicit nodes, edges, durable state, and check-pointing. RefractRouter uses LangGraph as the lower-level execution substrate for a fixed task DAG.
  3. Pydantic AI: Pydantic AI provides typed tool definitions and structured model outputs. It is useful when strict schemas are required, but RefractRouter v0.1 does not need it as a core dependency unless structured-output parsing becomes a bottleneck.
  4. DeepSeek Harness: DeepSeek Harness, or DSH, is an agent harness where the agent loop itself is a plugin. For RefractRouter v0.1, DSH is reserved for the outer validation environment, not the core routing loop.
  5. LLM routing research gap: Existing LLM routing work mostly selects one model for an entire request. RefractRouter studies whether selecting a model separately for each node in a task DAG can improve the quality-cost-latency Pareto frontier.
  6. Task decomposition boundary: Static task decomposition belongs to the application layer. The router receives the DAG as input and focuses on per-node model selection. Dynamic re-splitting is deferred until node-level routing is validated.
  7. Benchmark design: A useful routing benchmark needs fixed task DAGs, multiple candidate models, per-node and per-task scoring, cost accounting, and critical-path latency. The first benchmark should stay small enough to reproduce.
  8. Scoring rubric: The v0.1 scoring rubric weights requirement coverage, evidence accuracy, analysis depth, structure and readability, and HTML validity. Scoring prompts and rubric versions must be versioned with run records.
